items.description: Working time to fell one 30 cm DBH tree, by tool, experienced worker
items.note: Stone axes take roughly 3-4 times as long as steel (Saraydar & Shimada 1971); saw and chainsaw times from logging practice (Conway 1982). Hardwoods take about twice as long as softwoods. Order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: Timber felled per worker per 8 h day
items.note: Includes limbing and walking between trees; depends strongly on tree size and terrain. Order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: Excavation by pick and shovel per worker per 8 h day
items.note: Labour-based road-works task rates; throwing the spoil more than ~4 m adds time.

items.description: Ore broken and hauled by hand per artisanal miner per day
items.note: Hand drilling, blasting or fire-setting and hauling; widely variable with rock hardness and depth. Order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: Gravel processed per person per 8-10 h day
items.note: A pan holds ~0.006-0.01 m3; an experienced panner washes 50-100 pans a day. Yield = in-place grade x volume x recovery.

items.description: Fraction of contained gold recovered by gravity methods
items.note: Fine (< 0.1 mm) gold is lost readily from pans and sluices; field practice figures, order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: Fraction of gold in milled ore recovered, by process
items.note: Artisanal amalgamation from Veiga et al. (2006); cyanidation from Marsden & House (2006).

items.description: Charcoal produced per mass of oven-dry wood, by kiln
items.note: Charcoal is ~75-85% fixed carbon; the remaining wood carbon leaves as CO2, CO, methane and tars.

items.description: Bloomery iron smelting ratios (experimental and archaeological)
items.note: Experimental reconstructions vary widely with ore richness and furnace operation; order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: On-site labour to build a single-storey timber-frame house, per m2 of floor area
items.note: Skilled trades with power tools; hand tools only roughly double it.

items.description: Diesel consumption of an agricultural tractor per kWh of PTO work
items.note: Lowest at full load; rises at part load.

items.description: Fuel consumption of a light 4WD pickup or SUV
items.note: Sealed-road values from EPA combined ratings; unsealed and off-road factors (1.2-2x) are field practice (low confidence).

items.description: Practical travel speed of a light 4WD by surface
items.note: Field-practice figures for safe travel, not EPA test data; order-of-magnitude only.

items.description: Minimum luminous efficacy of a qualifying omnidirectional LED lamp
items.note: Lamps with CRI below 90; a household 800 lm (60 W-equivalent) LED lamp draws about 10 W at this efficacy.

items.description: Lumen-method utilisation factor of a small domestic room: the fraction of lamp output reaching the working plane
items.note: Small rooms with light walls and ceiling-mounted lamps; the factor falls with room index and surface darkness.

items.description: Minimum average daylight factor recommended for rooms of a dwelling
items.note: Average daylight factor: indoor horizontal illuminance as a fraction of the simultaneous unobstructed outdoor illuminance under an overcast sky.

items.description: Depth of hand-dug artisanal alluvial diamond/gold pits and overburden, Sierra Leone, and of hand-sunk artisanal vertical shafts; columns are low and high ends
items.note: nmjd_kpcsc_2021, PDF p. 12: 'In 9 out of 21 sites an average excavation depth of 5 metres was reached, while pits in 4 sites have reached or exceeded the government stipulated 10 metre maximum depth for artisanal mining.' levin_gola_2013 (rows 1-3): 'Diggers estimate most pits are three-shovels deep, or about 3-4 metres' (p. 34); 'the typical three metres (or more) at other sites in the region and five metres in Kono' (p. 7); 'the average depth of overburden appears to be less in Kenema than in Kono (3 metres compared to 5 metres, respectively)' (p. 41). rupprecht_shaft (last row, Introduction): 'Artisanal miners are well experienced in manually digging vertical shafts of 10 m to 20 m in depth. Beyond this depth, it beocomes difficult for artisanal miners to access the deposit due to the depth, ventilation, and ground water.'

items.description: Excavated or inside diameter of a hand-dug circular shaft (hand-dug well; no artisanal mining source with a diameter was found)
items.note: fao_koegel_1985, sec. 5.2: 'The inside diameter of hand dug wells normally ranges between one and two metres.' ... 'the vast majority of dug wells are found to have diameters in the range of 1.2 to 1. 5 metres (4 to 5 feet).' wateraid_2013, p. 2: 'an excavation of about 1.5 metres in diameter provides adequate working space for the diggers and will allow a final internal diameter of about 1.2 metres after the well has been lined.' Water-well analogue, not mining. Rupprecht's proposed small-mine shaft is rectangular 1.8 m x 2.4 m.

items.description: Hand excavation and lining rate of a vertical shaft by an organised crew (hand-dug well analogue), relatively loose non-caving soil
items.unit: m of depth per crew-day (crew size not stated)
items.note: fao_koegel_1985, sec. 5.4 (re-read 2026-10-23): 'While one metre per day could theoretically be excavated and lined, this is difficult to achieve consistently, especially at greater depths.' An upper bound for a crew of unstated size, not a per-worker rate. A quotation earlier attached here ('a team consisting of five workers ... can dig and line 1 meter per day') is not on the cited page and was removed; no source for the crew size or for an artisanal mining digging rate has been found, so hand shafts stay refused.

items.description: Designed advance of a small-scale (drill-and-blast, timbered) rectangular shaft; contrast to hand digging
items.note: Design Characteristics: 'a 1.8 m x 2.4 m rectangular shaft advance 0.8 m per day will produce 3.5 m3 or 9.3 t of broken rock per advance.' Labour: 'Overall advance, including platform installation is approximately 20 metres per month.' Timbered cycle: 'This equates to approximately 10 m advance per month.' Proposed design, not a survey of artisanal practice.
